input.rationale: Compliant with the preferred position: no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant binds Bluefly (Customer) anywhere in the agreement. Section 14.8 (Personnel) — the expected home for such a restriction — contains only each party's responsibility for supervising its own personnel, IBM's right to determine assignment of its personnel, and IBM's right to subcontract to Subcontractors and Affiliates. Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit" and "induce" return no hits, and "employ" appears only in definitional and indemnity contexts (employees of Customer/IBM), so none of the detection triggers ("shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce ... to leave") are present. Section 14.16 ("Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others") is a freedom-of-action provision, not a restrictive covenant. Because there is no clause to narrow, no redline and no counterparty comment are proposed; the duration (12-month) and general-solicitation carve-out checks are inapplicable as they presuppose an existing non-solicit. If a restriction is introduced via SOW or order document, we would hold to the fallback: mutual, 12 months from the end of the individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.
